# Finite-base power entropy: exact dual, face attainment and zonoid comparison

This note characterizes the proposed base-only energy. Its arithmetic
lower bound is inherited from the already proved weighted integer
centerpoint / balanced-submeasure theorem. It does not give a cap-depth
bound for the escort-selected continuous point. The actual failure of
maximizing this base energy is separately certified in
`candidate f3dc7a372eeb1eae`.

## 1. Definitions and the necessary minimal-face convention

Let P be a nonempty finite subset of an affine Euclidean space, with
strictly positive masses m_z, total M=sum_P m_z, and Q=conv(P). For now
p may be any point of Q. Let F_p be its unique minimal face, so
p is in relint(F_p), let P_p=P intersect F_p, and put

 V_p=span(F_p-p),  M_p=sum_(z in P_p)m_z.

Fix a real exponent N>0 (the proposed mixed application has N=d+1).
Define

 Omega_p={alpha in V_p: L_z(alpha)=1+alpha.(z-p)>0
                              for every z in P_p},
 E_p=inf_(alpha in Omega_p) sum_(z in P_p)m_z L_z(alpha)^(-N).  (1)

In rank zero take Omega_p={0}; then F_p={p}, P_p={p}, and E_p=m_p.
The finite-point set has no repeated base labels.

The same value is the infimum of the full-P expression with all full-P
denominators positive. To prove this, restrict any full parameter to
V_p; its face contribution is at least E_p. Conversely choose a linear
functional e which vanishes on F_p-p and is strictly positive on every
z-p outside F_p. Such an e exists because a face of a polytope is exposed.
Extend a face parameter alpha to the whole affine span and use alpha+t e.
For large t all full-P denominators are positive; the face terms stay
fixed and every other term tends to zero. This proves equality of the
two infima. If P_p!=P, the full-P infimum is NOT attained: its face
contribution is always at least E_p and all off-face summands are positive.
The zero off-face escort mass is therefore a genuine limiting convention,
not the value of a finite full-P parameter.

## 2. Unique relative attainment and escort identities

For positive rank, Omega_p is bounded. Indeed some relative ball of
radius r>0 centered at p lies in F_p. Every admissible alpha is positive
on its convex hull constraints, hence 1-r||alpha||>0. Its closure is
compact. Approaching its boundary makes at least one finite denominator
tend to zero and the corresponding positive-mass summand tend to infinity.
The objective is continuous, so it attains a minimum inside Omega_p.

Its Hessian on V_p is

 N(N+1) sum_(P_p)m_z L_z^(-N-2)(z-p)(z-p)^T,

which is positive definite because the offsets span V_p. Thus the
minimizer alpha_p is unique. All derivatives are finite sums, and its
stationarity is exactly

          sum_(P_p)m_z L_z^(-N-1)(z-p)=0.                  (2)

Define unnormalized escort masses e_z=m_z L_z^(-N-1) on P_p, and e_z=0
outside. Multiplying (2) by alpha_p and using L_z=1+alpha_p.(z-p) gives

 sum_z e_z= sum_z e_z L_z=E_p,
 sum_z e_z z=E_p p.                                       (3)

Consequently lambda_z=e_z/E_p is a probability vector with mean p,
strictly positive on every point of P_p and zero off F_p.

If p is an occupied mixed base with convex positive d-volume fibers K_z
and centroids g_z, all anchored inclusions supplied by their actual
convex hull imply

       y_p=sum_z lambda_z g_z in int K_p.                 (4)

Indeed each g_z is interior to K_z, and the Minkowski combination
sum lambda_z K_z is contained in K_p because sum lambda_z z=p.
It has a ball around the displayed centroid combination. Thus the
selector is a single actual mixed point (p,y_p), with no rounding and
without an affine graph of fiber centroids. Formula (4) assumes these
actual fiber inclusions; arbitrary unrelated convex fibers do not suffice.

## 3. Exact entropy dual without an optimization gap

Put s=N/(N+1), r=1/(N+1), and define the compact barycentric polytope

 B_p={lambda>=0:sum_P lambda_z=1, sum_P lambda_z z=p}.

Every feasible lambda vanishes off F_p: integrate the exposing functional
e from Section 1. The exact attained dual is

 E_p=max_(lambda in B_p)
          [sum_P m_z^r lambda_z^s]^(N+1).                 (5)

For any feasible lambda and any positive face denominator L, Holder gives

 sum m_z^r lambda_z^s
  =sum (m_z L_z^(-N))^r (lambda_z L_z)^s
  <=[sum m_z L_z^(-N)]^r [sum lambda_z L_z]^s
  =[sum m_z L_z^(-N)]^r,

because the barycentric constraints make sum lambda_z L_z=1. This proves
weak duality. At the escort vector from (3), the Holder equality condition
holds term by term, so equality is attained. The function
sum m_z^r lambda_z^s is strictly concave on the probability simplex, and
B_p is convex; hence its maximizing lambda is unique and is precisely
the escort vector. No Lagrange duality qualification is being assumed.

In particular E_p^(1/(N+1)) is concave as a function of p in Q: combine
two optimal barycentric vectors and use concavity of their objective.
Thus its superlevel sets are convex. This alone is not a mixed-depth
statement.

For an exact normalized entropy description, put pi_z=m_z/M and define
the order-s Renyi divergence by

 D_s(lambda||pi)=(s-1)^(-1)log(sum lambda_z^s pi_z^(1-s)).

Then (5) is equivalently

       E_p/M=exp[-min_(lambda in B_p)D_s(lambda||pi)].      (6)

This equation is a definition-level identity, not a citation-dependent
entropy theorem. Zero coordinates of lambda cause no problem because
s>0 and pi_z>0.

## 4. Exact comparison with the archived balanced-mass capacity

For p in P define

 T_p=max{sum_z q_z:0<=q_z<=m_z, sum_z q_z(z-p)=0},
 D_p=min{sum_(z in P intersect H)m_z:
                     H a closed affine halfspace containing p}.

Rank-zero halfspace traces are the whole space. In positive rank one
may harmlessly allow the whole space in the minimum. The attained T_p
is the balanced-submeasure mass, or unnormalized zonoid-depth capacity,
from `candidate b4c3b9c6a52059d2`, Section 1.
The exact relations are

                    E_p >= T_p >= D_p.                   (7)

Here is a direct proof of the first inequality. Let q attain T_p>0,
and use lambda=q/T_p in (5). Since q_z<=m_z,

 sum m_z^r(q_z/T_p)^s >=sum q_z/T_p^s=T_p^r.

Raising to N+1 proves E_p>=T_p. Moreover

 E_p=T_p  iff  p=(sum_(P_p)m_z z)/M_p,                    (8)

and in that case E_p=T_p=M_p. For the only-if direction, equality in
the preceding chain forces lambda to be the unique entropy optimizer,
which is positive everywhere on P_p. It also forces q_z=m_z wherever
q_z>0. Thus q equals all face masses, and its balancing equation gives
the claimed mean. Conversely that mean makes alpha=0 stationary and
optimal, while the whole face mass is a feasible dominated submeasure.
All feasible q vanish off F_p by the exposing functional, so no omitted
mass enters this argument.

For completeness, the second inequality in (7) is the archived finite
LP/Cavalieri argument. The exact LP dual is

 T_p=inf_a sum_z m_z(1+a.(z-p))_+.

For every a, integrate the halfspace masses of the levels
1+a.(z-p)>=t for 0<t<1; each level halfspace contains p. This lower
bounds every dual value by D_p, proving T_p>=D_p. The LP dual equality
has an elementary finite-dimensional separation proof in the cited
source; its primal is a nonempty compact polytope.

There is also a direct pointwise comparison: convexity at L=1 gives

 L^(-N)>=(1-N(L-1))_+  for L>0,

with equality only at L=1. Apply this at the attained denominators and
then the hinge dual of T_p on the minimal face. In particular the exact
nonnegative tangent defect

 b_N(L)=L^(-N)-(1-N(L-1))_+

satisfies

               E_p-T_p >=sum_(P_p)m_z b_N(L_z).          (7a)

This is another elementary proof of E_p>=T_p and of strictness whenever
alpha_p!=0. The excess energy is therefore not additional dominated
mass; it already contains this positive tangent defect.

The face convention does not change D_p: restricting any full halfspace
to F_p gives at least its intrinsic face depth; conversely any chosen
face halfspace can be extended and then shifted by a large negative
multiple of the exposing functional e to exclude every off-face point
without changing its face trace. Hence full and face depths agree.

The escort masses e_z are generally NOT a dominated submeasure of the
original masses. In fact

       e_z<=m_z for all z  iff  alpha_p=0.                (9)

If alpha_p!=0, relative interior of p ensures some offset has
alpha_p.(z-p)<0, so its L_z<1 and e_z>m_z. Conversely alpha_p=0 gives
exactly the face masses. A always-valid dominated rescaling is

 c_p=min_(P_p)L_z^(N+1),  q_z=c_p e_z,
 retained mass=c_p E_p.

It has the same escort centroid, but no lower bound of M/2^n is supplied
for this retained mass. Thus replacing T_p by the larger E_p does not
produce a larger retained mixed body.

## 5. The lattice maximum is inherited, with a sharp equality description

Suppose now P is complete in an affine lattice Lambda:

                   P=conv(P) intersect Lambda.

Let k be the number of parity classes modulo twice the direction
lattice occupied by P. The already proved finite weighted theorem in
`candidate 58dcf29bfb78a573`
gives a p in P with D_p>=M/k. Therefore

                  max_(p in P) E_p >= M/k.                (10)

If Lambda has rank at most n, k<=2^n and (10) implies the proposed
M/2^n bound. This is a CONSEQUENCE of the older atomic halfspace theorem
and the stronger archived balanced-submeasure capacity; it is not an
additional arithmetic assembly theorem. Completeness is essential for
that occupied-parity theorem and is retained here.
For an explicit failure without completeness, take the five vertices
(0,0),(2,0),(3,1),(1,3),(0,2) in Z^2, each of mass one. They are in
strict convex position, so every E_p=1, whereas M/2^2=5/4. The hull
contains other lattice points; this is not the positive-fiber base of
an actual convex mixed family.

The strict minimal-face refinement of that same proved theorem says
one may choose D_p>=M/k and M_p>M/k unless P consists of exactly k
vertices, all of mass M/k. Combining this with (7)--(8) shows

 max_P E_p=M/k  iff  P consists of exactly k vertices
                         and every mass is M/k.          (11)

Indeed if E_p>T_p then it is strictly above D_p>=M/k; if E_p=T_p,
equation (8) gives E_p=M_p>M/k. In the exceptional configuration every
minimal face is a singleton, so every E_p=m_p=M/k directly. The cube
base {0,1}^n with equal masses shows sharpness of the M/2^n bound.

Across the full continuous base Q, E_p<=M, with equality only at the
ordinary weighted base mean bar_z=sum m_z z/M. At that mean alpha=0
and equality holds. At any other interior p, the derivative at alpha=0
is nonzero and the strict minimum is below M; on a proper face, E_p<=M_p<M.
Thus if bar_z is integral, maximizing E over the occupied bases uniquely
selects bar_z and its escort continuous center is the true original mixed
centroid. This is the same reduction already identified for the archived
raw-moment/John selector in
`candidate 43892fde2d187dd5`, Section 7.

## 6. Exact practical limitation, with an actual independent certificate

For d=2, N=3, three centered homothetic triangle fibers with radii
1,3,4 at bases -1,0,1 have masses (1,9,16)V and actual midpoint
compatibility. At p=0 the minimizing denominators are (2/3,1,4/3),
the raw escort masses are (81/16,9,81/16)V, and

 E_0=153V/8,  T_0=11V,  D_0=10V.

The endpoint energies are V and 16V, so the energy selector uniquely
chooses base zero and its centered continuous point. The full actual
closed-cap certificate in
`candidate f3dc7a372eeb1eae`
has captured mass 5V, below the original OC target 52V/9. A separately
certified centroid in the large endpoint fiber meets that target. Thus
this is a selector obstruction, not an OC counterexample.

Even the explicit dominated escort rescaling above retains only
(16/81)(153/8)V=34V/9, far below M/2=13V. This makes the distinction
between entropy value and physical retained mass exact.

The inequalities (5)--(11), all escort membership facts, and the old
moment-body domain survive the counterexample. What fails is the
extra assertion that maximizing the base-only energy chooses a point
with the required original mixed halfspace depth, or that its value
can simply be multiplied by Gamma_d to obtain such a depth.
